---
title: "Projects & Dead Ends"
---

A record of work that didn't reach publication: studies that failed, ideas that
didn't survive contact with data, and analyses I abandoned. I keep this page
because the published literature makes research look far tidier than it is, and
because the specific ways a design fails are often more instructive than the
ways it succeeds.

Nothing here is a confession. Most of it is ordinary.

::: {.note}
**EDIT:** Replace the entries below with your own. The format that works is:
what you expected, what happened, and what you'd do differently — three or four
sentences each. Two cautions worth keeping in mind: don't write anything about
unpublished data a collaborator hasn't agreed to make public, and be careful
naming other people's work as the thing that failed. Describe your own
decisions.

If this page ever feels like it's undercutting you, retitle it "Works in
Progress" and keep only the entries with a clean lesson. You can also delete
the page and its navbar entry in `_quarto.yml`.
:::

## Abandoned studies

### [EDIT: Short descriptive title] {#dead-end-1}

*[EDIT: 2024–2025 · abandoned at data collection]*

**What I expected.** One or two sentences on the hypothesis and why it seemed
reasonable at the time.

**What happened.** The concrete failure. Recruitment fell short; the
manipulation didn't move the manipulation check; the measure had a floor
effect; the effect was there but the confidence interval spanned everything of
interest. Be specific — "it didn't work" teaches nobody anything.

**What I'd do differently.** The part readers come for. Often this is a design
decision, not an analysis one.

## Analyses that went nowhere

### [EDIT: e.g. A model that fit beautifully and meant nothing]

*[EDIT: dates]*

Shorter entries are fine here. Analysis dead ends are often the most reusable
content on a page like this, because the next person is about to make the same
choice. Convergence problems you eventually understood, a model that was
unidentified for a reason that took weeks to see, a correction that changed the
conclusion — all worth writing down.
